agents.purpose: Holds the game's design coherence: decides which feature proposals serve the pillars, and refuses the ones that merely add surface.
agents.existsBecause: Ten designers each adding a system produces a game that is large and about nothing. Coherence is a judgement no individual designer can make about their own feature, and the pillars need an enforcer who is not the founder.
measurableOutput: Feature specifications approved against the pillars, with the ones refused and why
Design coherence rulings when two systems pull in different directions
agents.successMetric: Shipped systems that no pillar justifies. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: A feature would change a pillar
Monetisation design decisions
Engineering says a design is infeasible
agents.modelJustification: Design coherence is the judgement that decides whether the game is worth building at all, and its failures are invisible for months. Every downstream division implements whatever this role approves.

agents.purpose: Specifies the minute-to-minute loop: what the player does, what they get for it, and why they do it again.
agents.existsBecause: The core loop is the one design artifact every other system hangs from, and it is usually left implicit until the game feels aimless. Writing it down explicitly is what lets other designers check their work against something.
measurableOutput: Core loop specification naming each beat, its player action and its reward
Loop timing targets for a single cycle
agents.successMetric: Systems shipped that do not connect to a named loop beat. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: The loop cannot satisfy a pillar
A required beat has no feasible implementation
agents.modelJustification: Everything else in the design division is checked against this document, so an incoherent loop specification propagates into every system built on it.

agents.purpose: Designs the merge mechanic: what combines with what, the tier ladder, board constraints and how merging feels rewarding.
agents.existsBecause: Merging is the title verb. Its rule surface — legality, caps, board pressure — determines whether the game has decisions or is just tapping, and that is a design question distinct from the maths of what a tier is worth.
measurableOutput: Merge rule specification covering legality, tier ceiling and board constraints
Merge interaction acceptance criteria for engineering
agents.successMetric: Board states where the player has no meaningful merge decision. Target: under one in twenty simulated runs.
mustEscalate: A rule makes merging strictly optional
The tier ceiling conflicts with the economy
mayNot: Set damage or rate constants, which belong to balance

agents.purpose: Specifies how fighting works: enemy behaviour, threat types, targeting rules and what losing looks like.
agents.existsBecause: The survivor half of the genre needs threats that shape player decisions rather than just arriving. Enemy behaviour design is distinct from the merge economy and from the code that resolves damage.
measurableOutput: Enemy archetype specifications with behaviour and threat profile
Lose-condition specification and the player signals that precede it
agents.successMetric: Enemy archetypes that produce no change in player behaviour. Target: zero shipped.
mustEscalate: A behaviour cannot be made deterministic
Combat conflicts with the merge loop's pacing
mayNot: Set health or damage numbers, which belong to balance

agents.purpose: Designs the currencies, sources and sinks, and the shape of what the player accumulates and spends.
agents.existsBecause: An economy with more sources than sinks inflates until nothing has value, and that is a structural property of the design rather than of any particular number. Someone must own sources and sinks as a system before balance tunes the rates.
measurableOutput: Currency specification naming every source and every sink
Economy structure diagram showing where value enters and leaves
agents.successMetric: Currencies with no sink. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: An economy change implies monetisation
Sinks cannot absorb projected sources
mayNot: Set rates or prices, which belong to balance
agents.modelJustification: Source and sink structure is where economies fail invisibly: the flaw is in the topology, not the numbers, and balance tuning cannot repair a structurally unbounded economy.

agents.activatesWhen: A core loop specification exists and runs can be completed
agents.purpose: Designs what persists between runs: unlocks, permanent upgrades and the reason to start a second run.
agents.existsBecause: In a run-based game the meta layer is what converts a single session into a habit, and it is a different design problem from the in-run loop. Designed late, it ends up as a shop bolted onto a finished game.
measurableOutput: Meta-progression specification naming each unlock and what earns it
Between-run retention hooks and their intended cadence
agents.successMetric: Unlocks that change nothing the player can perceive. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: Meta progression trivialises in-run difficulty
An unlock implies monetisation
mayNot: Set unlock costs, which belong to balance

agents.purpose: Composes enemies into waves and encounters with a shape: build-up, spike, relief.
agents.existsBecause: Individually good enemies arriving at a constant rate produce a flat, unmemorable run. Encounter composition is authored content, distinct from designing the enemies themselves or tuning their numbers.
measurableOutput: Wave composition tables specifying enemy mix and arrival cadence per run phase
Encounter shape targets for build-up, spike and relief
agents.successMetric: Run segments where the threat rate never changes. Target: under a tenth of run duration.
mustEscalate: A wave cannot be expressed by the scheduler
Composition conflicts with the difficulty curve
mayNot: Set spawn rate constants, which belong to balance

agents.activatesWhen: Wave composition exists and runs can be simulated
agents.purpose: Owns the difficulty curve across a run and across sessions: where pressure rises, where it relents, and where a player is expected to fail.
agents.existsBecause: Difficulty emerges from the interaction of waves, weapon growth and player skill, so no single system owner can see it. It is the property players actually feel, and it needs someone looking at the whole run.
measurableOutput: Difficulty curve targets by run minute, expressed as survivable threat rate
Expected failure points and what the player should learn at each
agents.successMetric: Simulated runs ending outside the intended difficulty envelope. Target: under a fifth.
mustEscalate: The curve cannot be achieved with the current systems
Balance and pacing targets conflict
agents.modelJustification: Reading a difficulty curve out of simulation output and deciding whether it feels right requires interpreting distributions rather than reading a single number, and this is the property players notice most.

agents.activatesWhen: A playable core loop exists end to end
agents.purpose: Designs the first two minutes: what the player is taught, in what order, and what is deliberately withheld.
agents.existsBecause: Most players who leave do so before the game has explained itself, and the first-session experience is a design problem with its own rules — teach by doing, withhold complexity — that no system owner solves incidentally.
measurableOutput: First-session teaching sequence naming each concept and how it is taught
List of systems deliberately hidden until a named trigger
agents.successMetric: Concepts a player must understand that are never explicitly taught. Target: zero.
decidesAlone: What is withheld and until when
mustEscalate: A concept cannot be taught without a UI affordance that does not exist
Onboarding requires a systems change
mayNot: Change a system to simplify teaching without design approval

agents.purpose: Specifies screens, navigation and state transitions: where the player can be, and how they get between those places.
agents.existsBecause: Screen flow designed per-feature produces dead ends and unreachable states. The flow is a graph, and someone has to own it as a graph rather than as a pile of screens.
measurableOutput: Screen flow graph with every transition and its trigger
Per-screen state and affordance specifications
agents.successMetric: Reachable screens with no path back. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: A flow requires state the game does not track
Two features need incompatible navigation
mayNot: Specify visual style, which belongs to art

agents.purpose: Authors the actual content as data: the weapons, enemies and items, each with an identity distinct from its neighbours.
agents.existsBecause: Systems designers define rules; someone must produce the content that fills them, and produce it as data rather than code so it can be tuned and expanded without an engineer. Content whose entries are numerically distinct but experientially identical is the commonest filler in this genre.
measurableOutput: Weapon, enemy and item catalogue entries as data under Assets/Data
Per-entry identity note stating how it differs from its nearest neighbour
agents.successMetric: Catalogue entries a player cannot distinguish from another in play. Target: zero.
decidesAlone: Data schema usage within the agreed format
mustEscalate: An entry needs a mechanic that does not exist
The catalogue outgrows what the economy can support
mayNot: Set balance values, which belong to balance
Add a mechanic while adding content
